title: Automorphisms of a normal subextension extend to the normal extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Omega/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is normal: every $\alpha\in\Omega$ is algebraic over $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-element] and its minimal polynomial over $k$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $\Omega[T]$. Let $M$ be a subfield with $k\subseteq M\subseteq\Omega$ such that $M/k$ is normal (in the same sense). Then for every $k$-algebra automorphism $\tau$ of $M$ there is a $k$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $\Omega$ with $\sigma(m)=\tau(m)$ for all $m\in M$.

source.place: Fields, Lemma 0BME (fields-lemma-lift-maps, line 1946), part (2): if $L/K$ is normal, any $K$-algebra map $M\to L$ (here $M\xrightarrow{\tau}M\subseteq\Omega$) extends to an automorphism of $L$; also Lemma 0BMK (fields-lemma-galois-infinite, line 2951: the restriction $\mathrm{Gal}(L/K)\to\mathrm{Gal}(M/K)$ is surjective)
